slot.brief: Two long parallel wires carrying currents in the same direction; ask how the attractive force per unit length changes when one current and the separation are both altered.

stem: Two long straight parallel wires carrying currents in the same direction attract each other with a force of $6\times10^{-5}$ N per metre length. The current in one wire is doubled and the separation between the wires is made three times. The new force per unit length is

verdicts.working: The force per unit length is given by F/L = (μ₀ I₁ I₂) / (2π d). Here, I₁ is doubled and d is tripled, so the force per unit length becomes (2/3) of the initial value. Thus, (F/L)' = (2/3) * (6 × 10⁻⁵ N m⁻¹) = 4 × 10⁻⁵ N m⁻¹.

working:
The force per unit length between the wires is $\dfrac{F}{L}=\dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$, so $\dfrac{F}{L}\propto \dfrac{I_1 I_2}{d}$.

With $I_1\to 2I_1$ and $d\to 3d$:
$$\frac{F'}{F}=\frac{2}{3}$$
$$F'=\frac{2}{3}\times 6\times10^{-5}=4\times10^{-5}\ \text{N m}^{-1}$$

Independent check: The force per unit length is given by F/L = (μ₀ I₁ I₂) / (2π d). Here, I₁ is doubled and d is tripled, so the force per unit length becomes (2/3) of the initial value. Thus, (F/L)' = (2/3) * (6 × 10⁻⁵ N m⁻¹) = 4 × 10⁻⁵ N m⁻¹.
solution:
Force per unit length between parallel currents: $$\frac{F}{L}=\frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}\propto\frac{I_1 I_2}{d}$$
With $I_1\to 2I_1$ and $d\to 3d$: $$\frac{F'}{F}=\frac{2}{3}$$
$$F'=\frac{2}{3}\times 6\times10^{-5}=4\times10^{-5}\ \text{N m}^{-1}$$
